lessons.title: Regions
lessons.summary: An AWS Region is a geographic area containing multiple Availability Zones.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: An AWS Region is a geographic area containing multiple Availability Zones.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Resources and service endpoints are often regional, while some services have global components. Select the intended region explicitly in automation. Regional isolation, latency, residency and service availability influence architecture and recovery design.

lessons.takeaway: Resources and service endpoints are often regional, while some services have global components. Select the intended region explicitly in automation. Regional isolation, latency, residency and service availability influence architecture and recovery design.

lessons.title: Availability Zones
lessons.summary: An Availability Zone is an isolated infrastructure location within a Region.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: An Availability Zone is an isolated infrastructure location within a Region.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Distributing workloads across AZs can tolerate some local failures when routing, data and capacity support failover. Multiple instances in one AZ do not provide AZ resilience. Cross-AZ designs also need to consider latency and transfer cost.

lessons.takeaway: Distributing workloads across AZs can tolerate some local failures when routing, data and capacity support failover. Multiple instances in one AZ do not provide AZ resilience. Cross-AZ designs also need to consider latency and transfer cost.

lessons.title: IAM roles
lessons.summary: An IAM role defines permissions that trusted principals can assume to obtain temporary credentials.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: An IAM role defines permissions that trusted principals can assume to obtain temporary credentials.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: The trust policy controls who may assume the role; permission policies constrain what the resulting session can do. Role assumption is not the same as permission to access every resource. Prefer workload roles over embedded long-lived keys.

lessons.takeaway: The trust policy controls who may assume the role; permission policies constrain what the resulting session can do. Role assumption is not the same as permission to access every resource. Prefer workload roles over embedded long-lived keys.

lessons.title: Least privilege
lessons.summary: Least privilege grants only the actions and resources required for a defined task.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Least privilege grants only the actions and resources required for a defined task.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: IAM evaluation combines applicable policies and explicit denies; organization and session controls can further constrain access. Start with the intended API and resource, then use conditions where appropriate. Avoid solving AccessDenied with broad administrator access.

lessons.takeaway: IAM evaluation combines applicable policies and explicit denies; organization and session controls can further constrain access. Start with the intended API and resource, then use conditions where appropriate. Avoid solving AccessDenied with broad administrator access.

lessons.title: S3 storage
lessons.summary: Amazon S3 stores objects identified by keys within buckets.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Amazon S3 stores objects identified by keys within buckets.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Objects are not ordinary mounted block-device files. Access policies, encryption, versioning and lifecycle rules govern different behaviors. Prefixes organize keys but are not traditional directories. Choose storage classes and lifecycle transitions around access and recovery needs.

lessons.takeaway: Objects are not ordinary mounted block-device files. Access policies, encryption, versioning and lifecycle rules govern different behaviors. Prefixes organize keys but are not traditional directories. Choose storage classes and lifecycle transitions around access and recovery needs.

lessons.title: EBS
lessons.summary: Amazon EBS provides block volumes for compatible compute workloads within an Availability Zone.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Amazon EBS provides block volumes for compatible compute workloads within an Availability Zone.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A volume's filesystem and application consistency are separate from the block service. Snapshots support recovery and copying workflows, but application-aware procedures may be needed. Verify attachment, device identity and mount state before modifying data.

lessons.takeaway: A volume's filesystem and application consistency are separate from the block service. Snapshots support recovery and copying workflows, but application-aware procedures may be needed. Verify attachment, device identity and mount state before modifying data.

lessons.title: Security groups
lessons.summary: Security groups provide stateful traffic filtering for associated network interfaces.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Security groups provide stateful traffic filtering for associated network interfaces.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Rules permit traffic; response traffic for tracked flows is handled statefully. They do not create routes or make an application listen. Evaluate source identities, ports and attached groups rather than assuming a subnet label determines access.

lessons.takeaway: Rules permit traffic; response traffic for tracked flows is handled statefully. They do not create routes or make an application listen. Evaluate source identities, ports and attached groups rather than assuming a subnet label determines access.

lessons.title: VPC subnets
lessons.summary: A VPC subnet is an IP range in one Availability Zone with associated routing and network controls.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A VPC subnet is an IP range in one Availability Zone with associated routing and network controls.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A public route to an internet gateway alone does not make every resource public; addressing and security controls also matter. Private workloads may use NAT or service endpoints for egress. Avoid overlapping ranges across connected networks.

lessons.takeaway: A public route to an internet gateway alone does not make every resource public; addressing and security controls also matter. Private workloads may use NAT or service endpoints for egress. Avoid overlapping ranges across connected networks.

lessons.title: NAT gateways
lessons.summary: A NAT gateway provides supported outbound address translation for private workloads.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A NAT gateway provides supported outbound address translation for private workloads.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A public NAT gateway needs appropriate routing and public-side connectivity. It does not accept arbitrary unsolicited inbound connections to private clients. Consider AZ failure behavior, connection limits and data-processing cost when designing egress.

lessons.takeaway: A public NAT gateway needs appropriate routing and public-side connectivity. It does not accept arbitrary unsolicited inbound connections to private clients. Consider AZ failure behavior, connection limits and data-processing cost when designing egress.

lessons.title: VPC endpoints
lessons.summary: VPC endpoints provide private access paths to supported services without routing that traffic through public internet egress.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: VPC endpoints provide private access paths to supported services without routing that traffic through public internet egress.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Gateway and interface endpoints have different routing, DNS and policy behavior. Endpoint policy is an additional control, not a replacement for service authorization. Verify DNS resolution and route selection from the workload.

lessons.takeaway: Gateway and interface endpoints have different routing, DNS and policy behavior. Endpoint policy is an additional control, not a replacement for service authorization. Verify DNS resolution and route selection from the workload.

lessons.title: Application Load Balancers
lessons.summary: An Application Load Balancer routes HTTP-family requests using listeners, rules and target groups.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: An Application Load Balancer routes HTTP-family requests using listeners, rules and target groups.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Target health determines eligibility, while listener rules select destinations. A healthy check path may not exercise the failing business operation. Inspect target reasons, ports, security groups and application responses together.

lessons.takeaway: Target health determines eligibility, while listener rules select destinations. A healthy check path may not exercise the failing business operation. Inspect target reasons, ports, security groups and application responses together.

lessons.title: Auto Scaling
lessons.summary: Auto Scaling changes group capacity according to configured policies and health replacement rules.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Auto Scaling changes group capacity according to configured policies and health replacement rules.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Desired, minimum and maximum capacity constrain behavior. Startup delay, health checks, quotas and available capacity affect how quickly new instances help. Scaling the frontend does not automatically increase a bottlenecked database's capacity.

lessons.takeaway: Desired, minimum and maximum capacity constrain behavior. Startup delay, health checks, quotas and available capacity affect how quickly new instances help. Scaling the frontend does not automatically increase a bottlenecked database's capacity.

lessons.title: CloudWatch metrics
lessons.summary: CloudWatch metrics are timestamped measurements identified by namespace, metric name and dimensions.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: CloudWatch metrics are timestamped measurements identified by namespace, metric name and dimensions.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Statistics and periods determine how data is aggregated. Missing data and delayed reporting need explicit interpretation. Select the correct dimension set and time window before comparing values or changing alarm thresholds.

lessons.takeaway: Statistics and periods determine how data is aggregated. Missing data and delayed reporting need explicit interpretation. Select the correct dimension set and time window before comparing values or changing alarm thresholds.

lessons.title: CloudTrail
lessons.summary: CloudTrail records supported account activity and API events for audit and investigation.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: CloudTrail records supported account activity and API events for audit and investigation.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Events identify actors, actions, resources and timing, subject to configured event coverage and retention. Management and data events have different collection requirements. Lack of an event in one view does not prove no action occurred.

lessons.takeaway: Events identify actors, actions, resources and timing, subject to configured event coverage and retention. Management and data events have different collection requirements. Lack of an event in one view does not prove no action occurred.

lessons.title: Shared responsibility
lessons.summary: The shared-responsibility model divides security work between AWS and the customer.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: The shared-responsibility model divides security work between AWS and the customer.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: AWS operates underlying cloud infrastructure; customer responsibilities vary with the service and include data, identities and configuration. Managed services reduce some operating tasks but do not make application authorization or data protection automatic.

lessons.takeaway: AWS operates underlying cloud infrastructure; customer responsibilities vary with the service and include data, identities and configuration. Managed services reduce some operating tasks but do not make application authorization or data protection automatic.

lessons.title: S3 versioning
lessons.summary: S3 versioning retains multiple versions of objects in a bucket.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: S3 versioning retains multiple versions of objects in a bucket.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Overwriting or deleting a key may leave earlier versions recoverable, with delete markers affecting the current view. Lifecycle policies can remove versions, so recovery depends on retention and permissions. Versioning is useful protection but not a complete independent backup strategy.

lessons.takeaway: Overwriting or deleting a key may leave earlier versions recoverable, with delete markers affecting the current view. Lifecycle policies can remove versions, so recovery depends on retention and permissions. Versioning is useful protection but not a complete independent backup strategy.

lessons.title: RDS availability
lessons.summary: RDS availability features provide managed database redundancy and failover options depending on engine and deployment type.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: RDS availability features provide managed database redundancy and failover options depending on engine and deployment type.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Multi-AZ configurations address availability, while read replicas commonly address read scaling or other recovery patterns. Client reconnect behavior, DNS and transaction retry semantics still matter during failover. Test the actual engine and topology.

lessons.takeaway: Multi-AZ configurations address availability, while read replicas commonly address read scaling or other recovery patterns. Client reconnect behavior, DNS and transaction retry semantics still matter during failover. Test the actual engine and topology.

lessons.title: Read replicas
lessons.summary: Read replicas serve replicated database data and can offload eligible read traffic.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Read replicas serve replicated database data and can offload eligible read traffic.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Replication lag means reads may be stale. Route consistency-sensitive reads appropriately and monitor lag under write load. Promotion changes topology and application routing; it is not the same operation as every managed failover mechanism.

lessons.takeaway: Replication lag means reads may be stale. Route consistency-sensitive reads appropriately and monitor lag under write load. Promotion changes topology and application routing; it is not the same operation as every managed failover mechanism.

lessons.title: Lambda retries
lessons.summary: Lambda retry behavior depends on the invocation source and delivery mode.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Lambda retry behavior depends on the invocation source and delivery mode.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Synchronous callers, asynchronous invocation and event-source mappings have different retry and failure handling. Duplicate processing is possible, so make handlers idempotent and configure failure destinations or queues as appropriate. Match timeout and concurrency settings to dependencies.

lessons.takeaway: Synchronous callers, asynchronous invocation and event-source mappings have different retry and failure handling. Duplicate processing is possible, so make handlers idempotent and configure failure destinations or queues as appropriate. Match timeout and concurrency settings to dependencies.

lessons.title: SQS visibility
lessons.summary: The SQS visibility timeout temporarily hides a received message while a consumer processes it.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: The SQS visibility timeout temporarily hides a received message while a consumer processes it.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A message becomes available again if it is not deleted before visibility expires. Choose a timeout aligned with processing and extend it when supported for long work. Consumers still need duplicate-safe behavior because delivery semantics can permit repeats.

lessons.takeaway: A message becomes available again if it is not deleted before visibility expires. Choose a timeout aligned with processing and extend it when supported for long work. Consumers still need duplicate-safe behavior because delivery semantics can permit repeats.

lessons.title: Dead-letter queues
lessons.summary: A dead-letter queue isolates messages that repeatedly fail processing under a configured redrive policy.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: A dead-letter queue isolates messages that repeatedly fail processing under a configured redrive policy.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: It preserves evidence and prevents poison messages from blocking normal progress. Alarm on arrival and investigate before replay. Fix the cause, validate replay safety and control replay rate to avoid recreating the incident.

lessons.takeaway: It preserves evidence and prevents poison messages from blocking normal progress. Alarm on arrival and investigate before replay. Fix the cause, validate replay safety and control replay rate to avoid recreating the incident.

lessons.title: DynamoDB keys
lessons.summary: DynamoDB primary keys determine how items are identified and distributed for access.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: DynamoDB primary keys determine how items are identified and distributed for access.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Partition-key design should spread load while supporting required queries; a sort key organizes related items within a partition-key value. Hot keys and unsuitable access patterns cannot always be solved by increasing aggregate capacity.

lessons.takeaway: Partition-key design should spread load while supporting required queries; a sort key organizes related items within a partition-key value. Hot keys and unsuitable access patterns cannot always be solved by increasing aggregate capacity.

lessons.title: KMS controls
lessons.summary: AWS KMS manages cryptographic keys and authorized cryptographic operations.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: AWS KMS manages cryptographic keys and authorized cryptographic operations.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Key policies, IAM policies and grants interact with service usage. Permission to read an encrypted object does not necessarily include permission to decrypt it. Key deletion and disabled keys can make data inaccessible, so lifecycle controls are critical.

lessons.takeaway: Key policies, IAM policies and grants interact with service usage. Permission to read an encrypted object does not necessarily include permission to decrypt it. Key deletion and disabled keys can make data inaccessible, so lifecycle controls are critical.

lessons.title: Secrets rotation
lessons.summary: Secret rotation changes credentials and updates consumers through a coordinated lifecycle.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Secret rotation changes credentials and updates consumers through a coordinated lifecycle.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: The new credential must be valid at the target and available to clients before old access is retired. Cache lifetimes and long-lived connections can delay adoption. Test rollback and partial-failure behavior rather than assuming storage update alone completes rotation.

lessons.takeaway: The new credential must be valid at the target and available to clients before old access is retired. Cache lifetimes and long-lived connections can delay adoption. Test rollback and partial-failure behavior rather than assuming storage update alone completes rotation.

lessons.title: Route 53 failover
lessons.summary: DNS failover changes answers based on configured routing and health behavior.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: DNS failover changes answers based on configured routing and health behavior.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Cached answers remain until their effective lifetime expires, and clients may cache independently. The destination needs enough capacity and current data. DNS steering does not move existing connections or guarantee application correctness.

lessons.takeaway: Cached answers remain until their effective lifetime expires, and clients may cache independently. The destination needs enough capacity and current data. DNS steering does not move existing connections or guarantee application correctness.

lessons.title: CloudFront caching
lessons.summary: CloudFront caches eligible responses at edge locations according to cache policy and origin behavior.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: CloudFront caches eligible responses at edge locations according to cache policy and origin behavior.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: The cache key determines which requests share a response. Omitting a necessary variation can serve incorrect content; excessive variation reduces hit rate. Distinguish cache TTL, invalidation and versioned object naming when deploying updates.

lessons.takeaway: The cache key determines which requests share a response. Omitting a necessary variation can serve incorrect content; excessive variation reduces hit rate. Distinguish cache TTL, invalidation and versioned object naming when deploying updates.

lessons.title: Cross-account access
lessons.summary: Cross-account access authorizes a principal in one AWS account to use resources in another.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Cross-account access authorizes a principal in one AWS account to use resources in another.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Role trust or resource policies and the caller's permissions must align; explicit denies still apply. Use narrowly scoped trust and conditions appropriate to the relationship. Verify caller identity before diagnosing the target policy.

lessons.takeaway: Role trust or resource policies and the caller's permissions must align; explicit denies still apply. Use narrowly scoped trust and conditions appropriate to the relationship. Verify caller identity before diagnosing the target policy.

lessons.title: Service quotas
lessons.summary: Service quotas bound resource counts, request rates or other usage within defined scopes.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Service quotas bound resource counts, request rates or other usage within defined scopes.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Some quotas are adjustable and others are fixed; scopes may be regional or account-specific. Monitor headroom before growth or failover. Retrying a quota failure aggressively usually adds noise rather than capacity.

lessons.takeaway: Some quotas are adjustable and others are fixed; scopes may be regional or account-specific. Monitor headroom before growth or failover. Retrying a quota failure aggressively usually adds noise rather than capacity.

lessons.title: Cost attribution
lessons.summary: Cost attribution assigns cloud spending to teams, products or environments.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Cost attribution assigns cloud spending to teams, products or environments.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Consistent accounts, tags and billing dimensions make allocation possible, subject to service support and activation behavior. Separate usage changes from price or discount effects. Optimize measured cost without sacrificing required reliability or recovery capacity.

lessons.takeaway: Consistent accounts, tags and billing dimensions make allocation possible, subject to service support and activation behavior. Separate usage changes from price or discount effects. Optimize measured cost without sacrificing required reliability or recovery capacity.

lessons.title: Disaster recovery
lessons.summary: Disaster recovery restores workloads and data after failures beyond normal availability mechanisms.

sections.heading: What it is
sections.body: Disaster recovery restores workloads and data after failures beyond normal availability mechanisms.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Choose backup/restore, warm standby or other patterns from RTO and RPO. Include identity, encryption keys, networking and external dependencies. Test restoration in the intended recovery location; a copied snapshot alone is not a recovered application.

lessons.takeaway: Choose backup/restore, warm standby or other patterns from RTO and RPO. Include identity, encryption keys, networking and external dependencies. Test restoration in the intended recovery location; a copied snapshot alone is not a recovered application.

commands.title: Caller identity
commands.definition: Returns the account and principal used by the CLI credentials.
commands.purpose: Confirm the target identity before diagnosing access or running changes.
commands.environment: Read-only API call; select the intended profile and region explicitly where required.
commands.interpretation: Account is the account ID; Arn identifies the user or assumed-role session.
commands.safety: Read-only API call; select the intended profile and region explicitly where required.

commands.title: Configured region
commands.definition: Reads the region configured in the selected profile.
commands.purpose: Detect an unexpected profile configuration before regional API calls.
commands.environment: Local read; inspect effective environment and explicit --region as well.
commands.interpretation: An empty result means this profile setting is absent; environment or command-line configuration can still override region selection.
commands.safety: Local read; inspect effective environment and explicit --region as well.

commands.title: Instance inventory
commands.definition: Retrieves configuration and state for selected EC2 instances.
commands.purpose: Check AZ, subnet, addresses and lifecycle state.
commands.environment: Read-only; replace INSTANCE_ID and use the intended account/region.
commands.interpretation: Reservations contains Instances; State.Name is lifecycle state, not application health.
commands.safety: Read-only; replace INSTANCE_ID and use the intended account/region.

commands.title: Security-group rules
commands.definition: Returns inbound and outbound rules for a security group.
commands.purpose: Check allowed sources, destinations, protocols and ports.
commands.environment: Read-only; verify attachment and routing separately.
commands.interpretation: IpPermissions is ingress; IpPermissionsEgress is egress. Group references are different from CIDR ranges.
commands.safety: Read-only; verify attachment and routing separately.

commands.title: Route tables
commands.definition: Finds route tables explicitly associated with a subnet.
commands.purpose: Inspect next-hop targets for workload traffic.
commands.environment: Read-only; follow up on the VPC main association if no explicit association is returned.
commands.interpretation: Routes show destination prefixes and targets; an empty result may mean the subnet uses the VPC main route table.
commands.safety: Read-only; follow up on the VPC main association if no explicit association is returned.

commands.title: Volume state
commands.definition: Retrieves EBS volume configuration and attachments.
commands.purpose: Check AZ compatibility and attachment before host-level storage diagnosis.
commands.environment: Read-only; attached does not mean mounted or application-consistent.
commands.interpretation: State describes volume lifecycle; Attachments identifies instance and device mapping.
commands.safety: Read-only; attached does not mean mounted or application-consistent.

commands.title: Target health
commands.definition: Reports load-balancer target health and reason codes.
commands.purpose: Diagnose requests failing through a target group.
commands.environment: Read-only; inspect check path, port and expected status alongside the reason.
commands.interpretation: TargetHealth.State and Reason distinguish initial, unhealthy, draining and other states.
commands.safety: Read-only; inspect check path, port and expected status alongside the reason.

commands.title: Scaling groups
commands.definition: Returns group capacity settings and instance membership.
commands.purpose: Check desired versus actual capacity during scaling problems.
commands.environment: Read-only; quotas and launch activity may explain a shortfall.
commands.interpretation: Compare MinSize, MaxSize, DesiredCapacity and instance lifecycle/health fields.
commands.safety: Read-only; quotas and launch activity may explain a shortfall.

commands.title: Alarm state
commands.definition: Returns alarm definition, state and reason.
commands.purpose: Understand what threshold, period and missing-data policy produced a page.
commands.environment: Read-only; use the correct region and inspect the underlying metric population.
commands.interpretation: StateValue is OK, ALARM or INSUFFICIENT_DATA; StateReason explains recent evaluation.
commands.safety: Read-only; use the correct region and inspect the underlying metric population.

commands.title: Recent account events
commands.definition: Retrieves recent matching management-event history.
commands.purpose: Find configuration changes near an incident.
commands.environment: Read-only; event history coverage is limited and does not include every data event.
commands.interpretation: EventName, Username and EventTime identify actions; inspect the embedded event for resource and error details.
commands.safety: Read-only; event history coverage is limited and does not include every data event.

commands.title: Queue attributes
commands.definition: Reads queue configuration and approximate message counts.
commands.purpose: Check visibility timeout, retention and backlog indicators.
commands.environment: Read-only; approximate counts are not an exact transactional inventory.
commands.interpretation: ApproximateNumberOfMessages is visible backlog; NotVisible represents in-flight messages, not completed work.
commands.safety: Read-only; approximate counts are not an exact transactional inventory.

commands.title: Bucket versioning
commands.definition: Reads the bucket's versioning configuration.
commands.purpose: Check whether earlier object versions may exist for recovery.
commands.environment: Read-only; verify actual object versions and lifecycle retention before promising recovery.
commands.interpretation: Status Enabled or Suspended describes versioning configuration; an absent status differs from enabled.
commands.safety: Read-only; verify actual object versions and lifecycle retention before promising recovery.

commands.title: Configuration source
commands.definition: Displays resolved CLI configuration values and their sources.
commands.purpose: Find an unexpected profile, region or credential source before calling other APIs.
commands.environment: Read-only; do not share even masked credential diagnostics unnecessarily.
commands.interpretation: Type and Location explain where each value came from; keys are masked but account identity still needs STS verification.
commands.safety: Read-only; do not share even masked credential diagnostics unnecessarily.

commands.title: Available profiles
commands.definition: Lists named profiles in local AWS configuration.
commands.purpose: Choose the intended configuration context for a task.
commands.environment: Read-only local inspection. Use --profile explicitly on subsequent commands when needed.
commands.interpretation: Each line is a profile name, not proof of current authentication or account identity.
commands.safety: Read-only local inspection. Use --profile explicitly on subsequent commands when needed.

commands.title: SSO session login
commands.definition: Starts the configured IAM Identity Center authentication flow.
commands.purpose: Obtain a normal CLI session for an authorized profile.
commands.environment: Authentication action; use your own authorized account and configured profile. Never paste tokens into shared logs.
commands.interpretation: Follow the displayed device/browser flow; successful login caches session material locally but does not validate every service permission.
commands.safety: Authentication action; use your own authorized account and configured profile. Never paste tokens into shared logs.

commands.title: Instance status checks
commands.definition: Retrieves EC2 system and instance status checks.
commands.purpose: Separate host/platform health from guest operating-system health.
commands.environment: Read-only API call; set intended account/Region and ensure EC2 describe permissions.
commands.interpretation: SystemStatus and InstanceStatus have separate checks; passed checks do not prove the application works.
commands.safety: Read-only API call; set intended account/Region and ensure EC2 describe permissions.

commands.title: Network interface detail
commands.definition: Retrieves interface addresses, attachments and associated groups.
commands.purpose: Trace the actual network attachment of an affected workload.
commands.environment: Read-only; output contains internal addressing. Verify Region and interface identity.
commands.interpretation: PrivateIpAddresses, SubnetId, Groups and Attachment identify addressing and placement.
commands.safety: Read-only; output contains internal addressing. Verify Region and interface identity.

commands.title: Subnet ACL rules
commands.definition: Lists network ACLs associated with a subnet.
commands.purpose: Check stateless filtering on both request and return paths.
commands.environment: Read-only; evaluate ephemeral return ports and both directions with the actual traffic flow.
commands.interpretation: Entries include RuleNumber, Egress, action and port range; lower matching rule numbers take precedence.
commands.safety: Read-only; evaluate ephemeral return ports and both directions with the actual traffic flow.

commands.title: NAT gateway state
commands.definition: Retrieves NAT gateway state, subnet and addressing.
commands.purpose: Check whether a planned outbound translation path exists and is available.
commands.environment: Read-only; correlate with routing, metrics and the originating subnet.
commands.interpretation: State describes the gateway lifecycle; available does not prove route tables or destination access are correct.
commands.safety: Read-only; correlate with routing, metrics and the originating subnet.

commands.title: VPC endpoint policy
commands.definition: Retrieves endpoint configuration, associations and policy.
commands.purpose: Investigate private access to an AWS service.
commands.environment: Read-only; endpoint policy is only one part of authorization.
commands.interpretation: ServiceName and VpcEndpointType identify the service/path; route tables or network interfaces depend on endpoint type.
commands.safety: Read-only; endpoint policy is only one part of authorization.

commands.title: Object metadata
commands.definition: Retrieves metadata for one object without downloading its body.
commands.purpose: Check object size, version information and encryption metadata.
commands.environment: Read-only; requires relevant access. Denial does not establish whether the object exists.
commands.interpretation: ContentLength is bytes; ETag is not universally a plain MD5 checksum, especially for multipart or encrypted uploads.
commands.safety: Read-only; requires relevant access. Denial does not establish whether the object exists.

commands.title: Retained object versions
commands.definition: Lists retained versions and delete markers matching a prefix.
commands.purpose: Identify a recovery candidate after accidental overwrite or deletion.
commands.environment: Read-only; inspect the exact key and retained version before any restoration.
commands.interpretation: VersionId, IsLatest and LastModified distinguish versions; prefix can match more than one exact object key.
commands.safety: Read-only; inspect the exact key and retained version before any restoration.

commands.title: Bucket public-access guardrails
commands.definition: Retrieves bucket-level Block Public Access settings.
commands.purpose: Review guardrails during an exposure investigation.
commands.environment: Read-only; this output alone is not a complete effective-access audit.
commands.interpretation: Four booleans describe controls on public ACLs and policies; account-level controls and access policies also matter.
commands.safety: Read-only; this output alone is not a complete effective-access audit.

commands.title: Bucket encryption defaults
commands.definition: Reads the bucket's default server-side encryption configuration.
commands.purpose: Check the encryption policy applied to new uploads by default.
commands.environment: Read-only; defaults do not retroactively prove the encryption state of every existing object.
commands.interpretation: SSEAlgorithm identifies the configured mechanism; KMS settings may name a key.
commands.safety: Read-only; defaults do not retroactively prove the encryption state of every existing object.

commands.title: Database instance configuration
commands.definition: Retrieves RDS instance state and configuration.
commands.purpose: Inspect availability, endpoint and backup settings during diagnosis.
commands.environment: Read-only; available does not prove client connectivity or query correctness.
commands.interpretation: DBInstanceStatus is lifecycle state; Endpoint, MultiAZ and BackupRetentionPeriod describe separate properties.
commands.safety: Read-only; available does not prove client connectivity or query correctness.

commands.title: Lambda configuration
commands.definition: Reads a function's runtime, limits and execution configuration.
commands.purpose: Investigate timeout, memory or deployment configuration changes.
commands.environment: Read-only but output may contain environment variables. Protect secrets and verify function version/alias context.
commands.interpretation: Timeout is seconds; MemorySize is MB; LastUpdateStatus reports configuration update progress.
commands.safety: Read-only but output may contain environment variables. Protect secrets and verify function version/alias context.

commands.title: DynamoDB table state
commands.definition: Retrieves table metadata, key schema and capacity-mode information.
commands.purpose: Check the intended schema and resource state during throttling investigation.
commands.environment: Read-only; inspect metrics for actual hot-key or throughput behavior.
commands.interpretation: TableStatus describes lifecycle; KeySchema names partition/sort keys. ItemCount is an approximate periodically updated value.
commands.safety: Read-only; inspect metrics for actual hot-key or throughput behavior.

commands.title: Encryption key metadata
commands.definition: Retrieves KMS key metadata without performing decryption.
commands.purpose: Check key state, origin and intended usage.
commands.environment: Read-only; an enabled key can still deny a caller through policy or conditions.
commands.interpretation: KeyState can be Enabled, Disabled or another lifecycle state; KeyUsage identifies permitted operation class.
commands.safety: Read-only; an enabled key can still deny a caller through policy or conditions.

commands.title: Secret rotation metadata
commands.definition: Retrieves secret metadata without the secret value.
commands.purpose: Check rotation settings and version staging during credential incidents.
commands.environment: Read-only metadata; do not use get-secret-value merely to diagnose staging information.
commands.interpretation: RotationEnabled and VersionIdsToStages show configuration and version labels, not whether every consumer refreshed.
commands.safety: Read-only metadata; do not use get-secret-value merely to diagnose staging information.

commands.title: DNS record inventory
commands.definition: Lists DNS record sets in a hosted zone.
commands.purpose: Check configured routing records before comparing resolver answers.
commands.environment: Read-only; the hosted zone may be public or private. Configuration is not proof all caches updated.
commands.interpretation: Name, Type and TTL identify records; alias targets use different fields and do not expose a normal record TTL here.
commands.safety: Read-only; the hosted zone may be public or private. Configuration is not proof all caches updated.

debugging.title: AccessDenied with valid credentials
debugging.symptom: A workload authenticates but an AWS API operation is denied.

steps.evidence: Confirm the actual role, account, action and resource. Inspect identity/resource policies, relevant conditions and explicit-deny controls rather than only the attached allow policy.
Correct the narrowly missing permission or trust relationship in code. Do not grant administrator access to conceal an unexplained deny.
Repeat the intended operation with the workload identity and verify access to unrelated resources remains denied.

references.title: AccessDenied with valid credentials — primary documentation

debugging.title: Private instance cannot reach internet
debugging.symptom: A private workload cannot download required updates.

steps.evidence: Check the effective subnet route including the main table, NAT path, public-side routing, security controls and DNS. Distinguish DNS failure from TCP egress failure.
Repair the specific route or egress dependency. Prefer a service endpoint for supported private service access when that matches the design.
Test name resolution and the required outbound request from the workload while preserving inbound isolation.

references.title: Private instance cannot reach internet — primary documentation

debugging.title: ALB returns 503
debugging.symptom: An Application Load Balancer has no usable backend for a route.

steps.evidence: Inspect target registration, health reasons, listener routing and target ports. Compare the check path with actual application readiness.
Restore healthy targets or correct routing/check configuration without masking a broken application. Keep enough capacity during replacement.
Verify target health and representative requests through the same listener and hostname clients use.

debugging.title: Scaling does not add capacity
debugging.symptom: An Auto Scaling group wants more instances but remains below desired capacity.

steps.evidence: Inspect scaling activity, launch-template errors, quotas, subnet address availability and instance health failures.
Fix the evidenced launch or capacity constraint; use approved alternate capacity where needed. Avoid increasing desired count repeatedly without resolving the blocker.
Confirm new instances become healthy and workload latency improves, not merely that instance count rises.

references.title: Scaling does not add capacity — primary documentation

debugging.title: S3 object unexpectedly unavailable
debugging.symptom: An object read fails after a deployment or cleanup.

steps.evidence: Check key spelling, caller permissions, delete markers, lifecycle rules and encryption-key access. Access errors can obscure whether an object exists.
Restore the intended retained version if appropriate or repair the specific access rule. Do not make the bucket public as a diagnostic shortcut.
Read the intended object as the application role and confirm its version/content and restricted access.

references.title: S3 object unexpectedly unavailable — primary documentation

debugging.title: Duplicate queue processing
debugging.symptom: Customers receive duplicate effects from an SQS consumer.

steps.evidence: Compare processing duration with visibility timeout and inspect retry/delete behavior. Delivery semantics require duplicate-safe processing even without an obvious timeout.
Make the business operation idempotent, tune or extend visibility appropriately and delete only after successful processing.
Replay a message and simulate a worker interruption in a safe test; confirm one intended business effect and bounded retries.

debugging.title: Dead-letter queue grows
debugging.symptom: Messages repeatedly fail and accumulate in a DLQ.

steps.evidence: Inspect representative failed payloads securely, consumer errors and recent schema changes. Determine whether failures are poison messages or a shared dependency outage.
Fix the consumer or dependency, then redrive a small verified batch with rate limits and duplicate protection.
Confirm replayed messages complete, DLQ growth stops and normal queue latency remains acceptable.

debugging.title: KMS decryption denied
debugging.symptom: The application can locate encrypted data but cannot decrypt it.

steps.evidence: Check key state, region, key policy, IAM permissions and encryption-context conditions. Data-read permission and decrypt permission are separate.
Restore the intended key availability or narrowly correct policy/context usage. Do not create a new unrelated key expecting it to decrypt old ciphertext.
Read and decrypt as the actual workload identity and confirm unauthorized identities remain blocked.

debugging.title: Database failover leaves application errors
debugging.symptom: RDS has completed failover but the application still reports connection failures.

steps.evidence: Inspect endpoint resolution, stale pooled connections, retry deadlines and database health. Existing connections may not move to the new writer.
Refresh invalid connections and use bounded reconnect behavior compatible with transaction idempotency. Avoid replaying uncertain writes blindly.
Execute representative reads and writes through the normal endpoint and verify consistency and error-rate recovery.

references.title: Database failover leaves application errors — primary documentation

debugging.title: DR restore misses objective
debugging.symptom: A regional recovery restores resources but not a usable service within the target time.

steps.evidence: Verify recovery-account access, data freshness, keys, quotas, DNS and dependency order. Measure the complete path rather than only snapshot restore time.
Fix the slow or missing recovery steps in infrastructure and runbooks, and preprovision justified prerequisites for the required RTO/RPO.
Repeat an isolated recovery exercise and record successful user transactions, recovered data age and end-to-end elapsed time.

references.title: DR restore misses objective — primary documentation
